npm:jszip.reason: MIT is the permissive branch; the GPL branch would impose copyleft on the bundle.

npm:dompurify.reason: Apache-2.0 avoids MPL file-level copyleft, which webpack bundling makes awkward to reason about, and adds an express patent grant.

npm:harmony-reflect.reason: Same reasoning as dompurify; MPL-1.1 is also superseded.

nuget:CsvHelper.reason: MS-PL is GPL-incompatible (section 3(C) reciprocity cannot be satisfied alongside the GPL) and CsvHelper links into ParanextDataProvider, whose own source is AGPL-3.0-or-later. Apache-2.0 is explicitly GPLv3/AGPLv3 compatible and carries an express patent grant. See LICENSING.md.

exceptionsNote: STATUS: every entry in "exceptions" below was drafted by automated analysis of the named package's own licence file and has since been reviewed and signed off; the "reviewer" and "date" fields name who signed each one off and when. Each entry's "reason" states what is actually in that file, so a later reader can check it against the package without repeating the reading. An exception is the instrument that lets a package past the gate, so a NEW entry is a code-review question rather than a build one: the gate treats it exactly like any other, and it is hash-pinned, so the block returns the moment the package changes its licence text.

exceptions.reason: LICENSE is the MIT grant with one clause added between the permission notice and the warranty disclaimer, requiring a substantially altered redistribution to replace the original author's bug-reporting addresses; that is an attribution requirement rather than a use restriction, and the modified text identifies as no single license.

LICENSE holds two grants in one file - BSD-3-Clause for chroma.js itself and Apache-2.0 for the colorbrewer2.org colour tables it embeds - which is exactly the conjunction its package.json declares; no single-licence matcher identifies a two-grant document, and both operands are on the allowed list.

LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause whose non-endorsement clause reads 'The names of any contributors' rather than the canonical wording, above a two-line copyright and below a trailing contributors pointer; the grant is the declared BSD-3-Clause.

LICENSE is the canonical MIT text; only its copyright notice wrapping onto a second line defeats licensee's normalizer, which strips one copyright line and leaves the continuation behind as unmatched prose.

LICENSE.markdown concatenates the complete MIT and GPL-3.0 texts into one document, so no single-licence matcher identifies it and the recorded election cannot reach a verdict that requires identified text; this project takes the MIT branch of the declared choice, per the elections entry for npm:jszip.

LICENSE is lodash's compound document: a contributions preamble, the MIT grant covering all parts of the software, a CC0 waiver covering only sample code shown in the documentation prose, and a pointer to node_modules/vendor directories the published tarball does not contain. The grant over the shipped code is MIT.
LICENSE is lodash's compound document (see npm:lodash@4.18.1), differing only in the copyright holder line; the grant over the shipped code is MIT.
LICENSE is lodash's compound document (see npm:lodash@4.18.1), differing only in the copyright holder line; the grant over the shipped code is MIT.

LICENSE is the ISC grant for the package, followed by an MIT grant covering the named icons derived from the Feather project; two grants in one file identify as neither, and both are on the allowed list.
LICENSE is the MIT text introduced as 'the MIT/X11 license' beneath a copyright line, which licensee's normalizer leaves as unmatched preamble; the grant is the declared MIT.

package.json declares a conjunction rather than a choice, and correctly so: pako is a JavaScript port of zlib, so the zlib terms bind on the ported algorithm alongside MIT on pako's own code. No election can resolve a conjunction, both operands are permissive and on the allowed list, and the LICENSE the package ships carries only the MIT half, which is therefore the only text reproduced for it.

package.json declares MIT but the LICENSE the package ships is the BSD 3-Clause text (Copyright (c) 2022, Slab, Inc.). The file is the grant and the manifest field is wrong, so the verdict rests on the text; both licences are permissive and on the allowed list, and the discrepancy should be reported upstream.

LICENSE is Node.js's own two-part licence document - the Node.js contributors' MIT grant followed by Joyent's MIT grant for the parts originating in joyent/node - which identifies as neither on its own; both parts are MIT.

LICENSE is BSD-3-Clause whose non-endorsement clause names the Mozilla Foundation and project contributors rather than using the canonical wording, under a leading blank line; the grant is the declared BSD-3-Clause.
LICENSE is Node.js's own two-part licence document (see npm:readable-stream@2.3.8); both parts are MIT.
LICENSE is the canonical MIT text; only its three-line copyright block - two holders on their own bulleted lines - defeats licensee's normalizer, which strips a single copyright line.

nuget:Microsoft.ICU.ICU4C.Runtime.note: Windows only. Permissive; requires the Unicode copyright and permission notice to travel with copies.

nuget:Spart.reason: Its nuspec carries the pre-SPDX <licenseUrl> https://opensource.org/licenses/Zlib, which is OSI's page for the zlib License, so the determination is the SPDX identifier Zlib - already on the allowed list, and the canonical text is reproduced on the package's behalf.

nuget:Icu4c.Win.Min.reason: Its nuspec carries the pre-SPDX <licenseUrl> https://github.com/sillsdev/icu4c/blob/trunk/license.html. Deliberately free text rather than a bare SPDX identifier: which Unicode licence applies depends on the ICU release, and the closure resolves ICU 59 here. ICU moved to Unicode-DFS-2016 at ICU 58 and to the Unicode License v3 (Unicode-3.0) only at ICU 74, so recording Unicode-3.0 would reproduce that text on this package's behalf - a specific, wrong licence text in a legal document, which is worse than the admitted gap. Closing it needs the actual terms at that URL read and the matching SPDX text checked in.

nuget:System.Net.Http.reason: Its nuspec carries the pre-SPDX <licenseUrl> http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=329770, which is the MICROSOFT SOFTWARE LICENSE TERMS for the .NET Library - a named Microsoft licence with no SPDX identifier and no canonical text in the corpus, so it is recorded as free text and nothing is reproduced for it.
